subject: Combining display and closed storage
hook: How much open shelving is too much? A simple rule keeps it from looking cluttered.
fb:
A question that comes up a lot while we are planning living-room storage: how much open shelving is too much?

Our rule of thumb is to keep most storage closed and give open shelves only to the things you actually enjoy looking at. Display at eye level, everyday clutter behind doors below.

And here is a quick test with the hosting season coming up: if you would have to tidy a shelf before guests arrive, whatever is on it probably belongs behind a door.

gbp:
How much open shelving is too much?

It is one of the most common questions when we design alcove units, bookcases and living-room storage. Our rule of thumb: keep most of your storage closed, and give open shelves only to the things you genuinely enjoy seeing.

A few principles that help:
- Put display shelves at eye level and closed cupboards below
- Use doors for anything everyday, such as chargers, paperwork and games
- Leave a ledge on top of the cupboards for a lamp or drinks
- Use adjustable shelves so the display can change over time

A quick test: if you would need to tidy a shelf before guests arrive, it probably belongs behind a door.
